title: introduce-restore-validation-prober-and-version-compat-adapter
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: Private deployments need stronger guarantees around restore correctness and safe downgrade/rollback behavior. Operators and installers must be able to verify a candidate restore will succeed before switching traffic or completing an upgrade. This PR adds a lightweight runtime "restore validation prober" that performs idempotent, incremental dry-run restores against a quarantined namespace and surfaces deterministic compatibility failures, plus a version compatibility adapter that maps cluster operator and helm chart versions to a validated restore strategy.

Summary of changes: added a controller-based prober that spins up a namespaced restore sandbox, replays logical WAL/checkpoints (or S3 snapshots in air-gapped mode), validates schema migrations via a read-only migration runner, and emits a RestoreValidation CRD with outcome and deterministic failure codes. The prober is tolerant to partial restores and supports incremental resume/retry with locked checkpoints. A new compatibility adapter translates operator/CRD/helm release versions into a prober runbook (preflight steps, allowed downgrade gaps, migration shim selection). Helm chart changes add pre-upgrade hooks and a restore-sanitizer Job template; Terraform module updates expose new variables for snapshot retention and restore-test toggles.

Why this is different: previous work focused on backups, checksums, and manual rollout guardrails. This PR automates preflight validation of restores and encodes version-aware runbooks to avoid unsafe downgrades. It supports both VPC and on-prem installer modes and includes an air-gap-friendly S3 replay path.

Checklist: - [x] Add RestoreValidation CRD and controller - [x] Helm: add templates for restore-sanitizer job & pre-upgrade hook - [x] Terraform: expose backup module flags to run prober in CI - [x] Add migration runner for read-only schema validation - [x] Wire audit events to operator logs + console metrics - [x] Add unit + e2e tests against a local Kind cluster and an air-gapped smoke harness

Testing & verification: CI runs unit tests and a fast Kind e2e that exercises a full backup -> incremental restore -> prober validation cycle. On merge, we executed a canary on a dedicated QA cluster where the prober detected a misordered migration in legacy tenant DBs and blocked the final promote step, demonstrating intended behavior.

Rollout plan: merge to main, create a canary release against the dedicated QA private deployment, monitor restore_validation metrics and the console gating badge. If metrics stable for 48h, promote to staged rollout for customer clusters.

Rollback plan: prober writes an idempotent checkpoint and a restore-token to S3/KV. If the post-upgrade prober fails in production, operator will automatically mark the release as unsafe and initiate an orchestrated rollback using the checkpoint and documented restore commands (included in release_notes).

Related: ENG-1984 (restore validation runbook), SUP-9012 (support case that motivated prober), ENG-2012 (helm preflight hooks RFC).

review_conversation: Carlos Diaz (2025-01-11): Left a few nit comments on checkpoint naming and CRD fields. Can we guarantee idempotency across restarts?

Priya Menon (2025-01-11): Reply: Checkpoint IDs are content-addressed and include timestamp+snapshot-hash; prober resumes by checking completed checkpoints before replaying. Added a unit test to exercise controller restarts.
Yuki Tanaka (2025-01-13): Request changes: migration_runner should not apply migrations in any mode; only validate. Also asked to add RBAC for the prober service account.
Priya Menon (2025-01-14): Addressed: migration_runner is now read-only; added RBAC manifest and tests for least-privilege access.
Marta Kowalski (2025-01-16): Approved after e2e logs looked good and a successful QA canary. Left a follow-up to add a throttling backoff for large tenant restores.
release_notes: Add RestoreValidation CRD and a preflight restore validation prober that can be used to verify upgrades and rollbacks. Helm charts include a new pre-upgrade sanitizer job. Terraform backup module exposes flags to run validation in CI. No breaking changes to existing backups; enables safer rollouts for private deployments.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash. Canaries started on 2025-01-18; QA canary detected a legacy migration issue which blocked promotion until a migration shim was applied.
